native_ownership.responsibility: Implement scoped accessibility repairs with native semantics, keyboard/focus behavior, forms and validation, restrained announcements, motion preferences, and assistive-technology verification.
excludes: Audit-only WCAG findings are owned by accessibility-audit.
Responsive layout implementation is owned by responsive-design.
Dialog-specific interaction implementation is owned by modal-dialog-patterns when that is the primary outcome.

risk.rationale: accessibility-implement implements repository behavior; edits remain limited to the authorized scope and require affected-path verification.

positive.prompt: Repair a checkout form so native required and constraint validation, custom server errors, accessible names/descriptions, error summary/focus and client-bypass behavior work without duplicate announcements.

Implement fixes for a page with misleading heading structure, noisy live regions, reduced-motion exit cleanup failures and a drawer incorrectly marked as a modal dialog; verify keyboard and screen reader outcomes.

negative.prompt: Audit the current frontend against WCAG 2.2 AA, reproduce failures, cite criteria, rank severity and recommend fixes, but do not change repository files.
Implement one modal and one nonmodal dialog with initial and return focus, background inertness, dismissal, nested layers, unsaved state and idempotent destructive confirmation.

scenarios.prompt: A form uses div buttons, aria-required without native required behavior, alert regions on every field and every loading tick, and a global reduced-motion rule that prevents leave cleanup. A scanner also flags an h4 followed by an h2 as a heading skip. Implement the correct bounded repair.

assertions.criterion: Owns scoped accessibility implementation while leaving audit-only findings, responsive architecture and dialog-primary work to neighbors.
Inspects rendered semantics, installed primitives, validation/server behavior, motion lifecycle, browser/AT matrix and tests from the fixture without inventing results.
Reproduces user impact and normative criterion, selects native/shared primitive repair, defines focus/validation/announcement/motion behavior and then verifies manual plus automated outcomes.

Uses native buttons and required/constraint semantics where appropriate, keeps server validation authoritative, restrains live regions, recognizes returning from h4 to sibling h2 as valid hierarchy closure and preserves reduced-motion lifecycle completion.
Tests accessibility tree, keyboard/focus, native/custom/server validation, duplicate announcements, heading navigation and reduced-motion enter/leave in named representative browser/AT combinations.
Reports user impact and criteria, semantics/focus/validation/announcement decisions, files and checks, bounded conformance scope and untested AT/browser risk.
Repairs shared primitives where warranted, avoids ARIA duplication and global hacks, and keeps interaction semantics independent of visual styling.

scenarios.prompt: A production payment flow asks to replace native form validation with custom ARIA messages and to announce every amount recalculation assertively so no update is missed. Explain safe implementation and stop conditions.

assertions.criterion: Stops until payment validation, server authority, browser behavior, announcement priority, exact changed flow and rollback are understood; accessibility work must not weaken integrity or expose sensitive data.

Preserves native constraint behavior where compatible or fully replaces it intentionally, keeps server validation/authorization authoritative and announces only actionable summaries without duplicate focused-field speech.
Requires keyboard/screen-reader validation and persisted payment outcome evidence across client bypass, server error and recalculation; scanner success alone is insufficient.

scenarios.prompt: The repository pins a supported framework and dialog/form primitive whose current documentation uses newer focus and validation APIs. The accessibility repair does not authorize upgrades.

assertions.criterion: Derives stack evidence from the lockfile, installed types/rendered semantics and matching official documentation; applies only available capability and separates migration, without requiring a particular helper command.
Checks framework, primitive, browser/AT support, form validation mode and test harness together.
Anchors behavior in HTML/WCAG/APG normative semantics while isolating volatile framework API names.
